puzzles.title: The Same Book, Five Different Senders
puzzles.scenario: Within a year, a man receives the exact same novel five times in the mail, always secondhand, always from a different sender he doesn't know, and never with a note.
puzzles.solution: He mentioned the novel in passing in an interview months earlier, about recovering from a hard period in his life, as the book that got him through it. Members of an online support group who saw the interview each sent him their own copy, without knowing anyone else was doing the same.
puzzles.hint: Don't ask who the senders are — ask what they all happen to have read or seen.

puzzles.title: The Bins That Moved Themselves
puzzles.scenario: In an apartment building, every Sunday morning all the trash bins are already sitting neatly by each resident's door, empty and rinsed out, though no one admits to doing it and the municipal collection service certainly doesn't.
puzzles.solution: An older resident, a nurse for decades on an early shift, is awake by five and can't sit still. She wheels the bins out herself, waits for collection, and puts them back rinsed at every door afterward, never mentioning it because she doesn't think it's worth bringing up.
puzzles.hint: Who in this building is always the first one awake?

puzzles.matchTitle: Verse bloemen in een leeg appartement
puzzles.title: Fresh Flowers in an Empty Apartment
puzzles.scenario: The upstairs apartment has stood empty for six months since the previous tenant moved abroad, but fresh flowers appear on the windowsill every week, clearly visible from the street, though no one has ever seen the door open.
puzzles.solution: The estate agent still trying to sell the place refreshes the flowers before every viewing to keep it looking move-in ready. She schedules her visits just outside the building's usual quiet hours, using the spare key she got from the previous owner.
puzzles.hint: Who benefits from an empty home not looking empty?

puzzles.matchTitle: De stoel die nooit bezet raakt
puzzles.title: The Seat That Never Fills Up
puzzles.scenario: Every morning on a packed commuter train, the same seat carries a handwritten 'reserved' sign, though the conductor confirms nothing has ever been officially reserved and the train is standing room only.
puzzles.solution: A regular passenger made this commute for thirty years with his wife, until she passed away last year. The conductor, who knew them both, sets the sign down every morning before the man boards, so the seat beside him stays empty without him ever having to ask.
puzzles.hint: Don't ask who's claiming the seat — ask who it's being kept empty for.

puzzles.matchTitle: Water dat 's nachts stroomt in een slapend huis
puzzles.title: Water Running at Night in a Sleeping House
puzzles.scenario: A family's water meter has been logging a sharp spike in usage every night between three and four for months, even though everyone is asleep and a plumber can't find a single leak in the house.
puzzles.solution: Under the lawn sits an old, professionally installed irrigation system from the previous owner, never disclosed at the sale. After a power outage, the timer reset to its original factory schedule and now waters a flower bed that hasn't existed for years, in the middle of the night.
puzzles.hint: The water might be leaving the house before anyone ever uses it inside.

puzzles.matchTitle: Eén bloem op de ruitenwisser, elk jaar opnieuw
puzzles.title: One Flower on the Windshield, Every Year
puzzles.scenario: For more than ten years, a woman has found a single fresh flower tucked under her car's wiper blade on her birthday, always the same kind, always gone before anyone else could see it, even across three different addresses.
puzzles.solution: Her father did this every year while she still lived at home. After he died, her mother quietly kept the tradition going, learning her daughter's new address each time through ordinary conversation, and leaves the flower before sunrise on her way to a volunteer shift, never taking credit because it was always his habit.
puzzles.hint: Who would always know, year after year, where she lives now?

puzzles.matchTitle: De kat die de deur mijdt
puzzles.title: The Cat That Avoids the Door
puzzles.scenario: An indoor cat that has never once been outside refuses to go near the front door every evening around six, even though nothing in the hallway looks any different.
puzzles.solution: The downstairs neighbor's dog is walked past that door at exactly six every evening. The cat can smell and hear it through the gap under the door, even though its owner never actually sees the dog.
puzzles.hint: What can a cat notice through a closed door that a person can't?

puzzles.matchTitle: Twee kinderen bellen op dezelfde avond
puzzles.title: Two Children Call on the Same Evening
puzzles.scenario: For the first time in months, a mother gets a call from both her children within fifteen minutes of each other on an ordinary weeknight, though they live in different cities and hadn't spoken to each other that day.
puzzles.solution: That morning, without mentioning it, the mother had finally uploaded an old family photo to a shared album she'd been slowly digitizing for months. Both children got the notification around the same time and called independently, prompted by the same photo.
puzzles.hint: Did something happen today that both children saw at the same time, but separately from each other?
